newsitem.title: UK: UK's Aston Villa soccer club launches share offer.
newsitem.headline: UK's Aston Villa soccer club launches share offer.

text.p: British soccer club Aston Villa launched its bid for a London stock market listing on Thursday, asking fans and professional investors to pay 11 stg ($17.85) a share for a 15.9 percent stake, to value the club at 125.9 million pounds.

The sale should net 15.225 million for the club to spend on improving the Villa Park stadium and the team, as well as raising nearly four million pounds for chairman Doug Ellis, according to the flotation prospectus.

The prospectus said the club was selling 454,545 new shares in a public offering and placing a further 1,363,636 shares with institutional investors, including 363,636 existing shares owned by Ellis, who will be left with 33.4 percent of the company.
Earnings for the year ending May 31, 1997 are forecast in the prospectus to come in at 32.9 pence a share, putting the offer price on a multiple of 33.4 times earnings.
The notional net dividend for the year just ending is put at 8.8 pence, giving a notional gross dividend yield of 1.0 percent.

The club said it believed it could continue to increase commercial revenue to supplement match day income from sponsorship, merchandising, catering and its share of the premier league television broadcasting contract with BSkyB pay television.
In addition, the club plans to raise seat prices next season and also increase the stadium capacity from 39,000 to around 50,000.
"The flotation provides liquidity for existing shareholders and the chance for many more supporters to share in the growth and development of Aston Villa," Ellis said in a statement.

The club is forecast to make a taxable profit in the current year to May 31 of 2.78 million stg on sales of 21.164 million stg, after a 50,000 stg loss last year after spending a net 6.1 million stg on transfer fees.
There are already 15 British soccer clubs listed on the stock market.
